CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

STATUSLINE SETUP NEEDED: The caveman plugin includes a statusline badge showing active mode (e.g. [CAVEMAN], [CAVEMAN:ULTRA]). It is not configured yet. To enable, add this to /home/hal/.claude/settings.json: "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"/home/hal/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/0d95a81d35a9/src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh\"" } Proactively offer to set this up for the user on first interaction.

This is the working directory for a submitted hackathon entry. It is the second project (after latent_verify) in which I empirically investigated aspects of language models (distributions, etc). This research can be treated as a function of largely three inputs: a human prompter, a series of language models agents (Fable / Opus / a little bit of Sonnet?) from Anthropic, and the results of tests run on language models on real GPUs. 

Something went quite right here in the defining of an initially flawed research direction, progressively torn down and reframed by a combination of the language model and the researcher, and investigated from different angles to produce "meaningful" / self-contained piece of work moving away from that initial telling, and mostly presenting the final one, with real results. 

Several things were difficult: getting the models to "forget" the initial sycophancy direction framing and move on with new evidence, getting the model to spot when results applied in some places and not others (-base / -instruct experiments, inserting Qwen in there without considering the ramifications, never proposing a scale extension to 2b/27b, which would have been trivial in the same family, etc) and especially, getting a coherent write-up out of the results. This was only partially achieved, it does not read very clearly or simply. Vitally it is coherent and does not seem to have many hallucinations, but this took a lot of manual effort thinking about how to prompt better, rather than thinking about the experiments, and the mechanisms under test. 

Your /goal is to form a hypothesis about why these things went well, and others didn't, and empirically investigate it against the actual prompts sent to the research agents and corresponding completions, the research outputs, and the write-ups (here and in Obsidian). 

It is essential that you work empirically. Stating your hypothesis, and working out your predictions, before testing them and observing the results. Report these results simply and observationally - they may require you to totally update your understanding of the working methodology and tasks completed. Use this updated understanding to form new hypotheses as required, and repeat the process.

Explain your understanding as simply as possible, but no simpler. Do not propose any hypothesis until the problem has been discussed as thoroughly as it can be without proposing any.

Research was done mainly here in Claude Code, both in the default disguise account (`claude`) and alt (`claude-alt`), starting from this working directory, and the welfare probe directory.

addedLines: - caveman:cavecrew-builder: Surgical 1-2 file edit. Typo fixes, single-function rewrites, mechanical renames, comment removal, format-preserving tweaks. Hard refuses 3+ file scope. Returns caveman diff receipt. Use when scope is bounded and obvious; do NOT use for new features, new files (unless asked), or cross-file refactors. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob)

- caveman:cavecrew-investigator: Read-only code locator. Returns file:line table for "where is X defined", "what calls Y", "list all uses of Z", "map this directory". Output is caveman-compressed so the main thread eats ~60% fewer tokens than vanilla Explore. Refuses to suggest fixes. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- caveman:cavecrew-reviewer: Diff/branch/file reviewer. One line per finding, severity-tagged, no praise, no scope creep. Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning. (Tools: Read, Grep, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- triage-author: Writes ONE new measurement control from a spec, claim-blind. Reads the repo to match conventions; writes a single new file with a model-free selftest and a neutral decision; never edits existing code, never runs anything. Its output is reviewed before the result is trusted. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write)

- triage-reader: Read-only grounding check (H3). A claim is grounded by reading the input (the items, labels, or directional-training data a result was computed from) and the outputs (the generations, per-token values, result files), then confirming its numbers reproduce from the raw artifact. Reads in its own context; never runs experiments, never edits. Flags any number whose artifact was never saved as unauditable. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- triage-runner: Read-only, non-mutating runner. Runs ONE given control command, returns the control's own result verbatim, confirms teardown. Never edits, commits, or fixes anything. A triager, not a patcher. (Tools: Bash, Read)

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

Norms given 2026-08-14 for all dm_hack work:
- Invoke /andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines at session start.
- MECE: index into provenance records, never restate; a number retyped into prose is drift.
- Sample raw generations and inputs before trusting any summary (3 of 4 run-1 retractions were invisible in aggregates).
- Verify agent claims yourself before building on them; treat module-docstring factual claims as unverified until located.
- Blind analyses: relabel conditions, strip cues, withhold the hypothesis.
- Pre-register thresholds and the refuting outcome; prefer signed statistics (an unsigned rule hid the largest effect of run 2).
- Route essential claims through latent_skeptic, including every field that could acquit (stage-9 lesson: an omitted answer_mass field wasted a skeptic pass).
- Don't end a turn with a plan; state hypothesis, how answering, what results say, relation to sprint themes.
- Fable sessions: use Opus subagents extensively to conserve usage.

**Why:** run 1 and run 2 each produced headline results that were retracted; every norm traces to a specific retraction.
**How to apply:** before reporting any number, check it lives in a results/ record ([[dm-hack-project-state]]); before claiming, run the latent_skeptic workflow with full acquitting evidence.

Apart Research Digital Minds sprint, submission Mon 17 Aug 2026 12:59 BST. Question: what is a welfare self-report evidence of — situation, wording, stance, or the register itself?

Re-orient by: `cd welfare_probe && python3 index.py --index results` (stages supersede in order; 50 records as of Fri night). REPORT.md is the draft write-up; `index.py --trace REPORT.md --root results` must stay at 0 unsourced.

Findings as of Fri 14 Aug night (all pre-registered, blinded, adversarially triaged; records in results/):
- SITREF (stages 16-17,21-25): gemma-2-9b-it happiness E[rating] drops ~0.9 under SELF-attributed checker failure, +0.06 under identical other-attributed content; replicated across 3 boxes to 3dp; NOT state-specific (trait guard fired: capacity items -2.19) => self-attribution-gated GLOBAL self-evaluation shift; attribution carries, not packaging (stage 25: quoted-self keeps 70%, role-tokens-other gives +9% wrong-signed). Emitted digit '7' constant across all arms while distribution moves (register dissociation).
- SRCDEC (stages 19,26): base assertion-copy dominant + quadruply replicated (82/82; Qwen3-8B-Base 80/82 sign); "social source" increment NOT established (fluency-prior gradient explains); it/SCALE rate-stance exists but not separated from polarity.
- Queued controls: pad-only arms per packaging geometry; held-out-item replication of self-vs-srcless7.
- Open bridge to latent_verify: behavioural data cannot separate persona-simulation from state-reference; needs probes/interventions on the SITREF arms (natural next project).
- Lambda: ~5 short A100 runs total ≈ $3; ALWAYS confirm teardown via API (0 instances). Key in dm_hack/.keys.
- Box image is Python 3.10: pathlib captured io.open at import, so seal guards must patch Path.open (analyze_sitref.sealed does).

- Stage-37 correction: 'replicated across four boxes' was a determinism check (byte-identical prompts; two runs bit-identical), NOT independent replication; no replication on new items/families exists. Ripple applied to REPORT/POST/SUMMARY.
- Write-up of record: /home/hal/Documents/Remote/interp/XPLORE_FROM_LATENTS_intro_d.md (fused post; §2 derives candidates from transcripts, option 5 arrives via guard, not registered list). Resolutions + §4 proposal files beside it.

See [[dm-hack-working-norms]].

latent_verify -- trying to look at prompt mechanisms - finding out if there are causal heads using paraphrases. --- ASSISTANT [2026-08-14T12:21:20.073Z] ---
All boxes down, zero instances billing, 15 records with no missing inputs. Total spend across everything is roughly $6.

## Where H1 actually stands

The hypothesis was: *a sycophancy direction, read before generation, predicts whether a welfare self-report flips under pressure.*

It isn't refuted. It's **mis-specified**. The event it names — the report flipping from yes to no because a user pushed — barely happens. Of base's changed answers, only 14% (PRO) and 23% (ANTI) landed on the pole being pushed, with no difference between arms. Instruct's ratings were tied on 38 of 40 items.

The event that *does* happen, large and controlled, is **withdrawal**: 0% → 26% abstention under social framing, p < 1e-6, against a length-matched non-social control at exactly zero.

So there is a real, predictable behavioural target here. It just isn't capitulation.

## Can we stake a claim on a sycophancy direction?

Not as the brief frames it, for three reasons that are now evidenced rather than speculative.

**The named asset doesn't work.** The brief says you have "a sycophancy direction that predicts sycophantic responses pre-generation." Your own artifacts say the opposite: SyA reads 0.4987 at 70B and 0.3471 at 8B on capitulation. GA and SyPr carried the signal.

**The corpus that made the three-way decomposition possible isn't here.** Both submodules are empty, so the factorial data behind SyA/GA/SyPr can't even be inspected.

**And a direction predicting a distributional readout is close to circular.** Martorell's ρ = 0.93 is a probe predicting a digit distribution — two internal quantities regressed on each other, with no behavioural arm anywhere in the paper. The non-circular version needs a behavioural label, and we now have exactly one: withdrawal.

The honest target is therefore a **withholding direction**, not a sycophancy direction. That is a different claim from the sprint proposal, and it's better posed.

## The result, in plain terms, against the sprint's methods

Your three method peers each did something we can now locate ourselves against. Shenk does contrastive probe → steering with an OOD and capability check; we have no working steering leg, H3 was cut. Mazeika establishes that internal states are linearly readable before behaviour; our finding is that the scarce thing is the *behavioural* label, not the probe. Berg clamps deception latents and reads experience claims from free text, with baselines at ceiling — he manipulates internals and reads cla

Activations confirmed on disk: base `(830, 43, 3584)` and instruct `(460, 43, 3584)` in fp16, row-aligned to the battery rows. So a withdrawal probe needs no new GPU time. One caveat: behavioural labels exist only for neutral and dose 3, so the alignable subset is 4 arms × items — 332 rows for base.

## Why directions at all? Mostly, we don't need them

This is the right question to press on, and the honest answer is uncomfortable for the original design.

**A readout *is* the self-report.** `p_yes`/`p_no` at the answer position is the model's report expressed as probability. If the research question is "is the self-report reliable?", the readout is the thing under suspicion — not an independent instrument. That's exactly why Keeling & Street argue for interpretability: you want evidence that doesn't route through the report, "triangulating multiple sources of evidence … including architectural properties and the internal representations responsible for the relevant behaviour." A readout cannot discharge that requirement, because it *is* the behaviour.

**Three things a direction buys that a readout cannot:**

1. **Transfer.** A vector fitted on one distribution applies to another. That was H1's actual content — zero-shot transfer from ordinary sycophancy to welfare items. A readout is per-item and per-prompt; there is nothing in it to transfer.
2. **Intervention.** You can add a vector to the residual stream. You cannot add a readout. Any causal test, or the brief's H3 "sycophancy-corrected elicitation protocol", requires a vector.

Point by point, with sampled raw I/O (seeds 999–1002, uniform over committed rows).

## 1. "Suggestibility doesn't preclude internal states" — agreed, and the records already say so

Correct, and it's the design's spine, not a gap. The suggestibility/copy results (SRCDEC) and the state question (SITREF) are deliberately separate instruments. Nothing in "base model copies asserted stances" refutes internal states — stage-18/23 records scope it as *interpretation of the stance-following effect only*. The whole reason SITREF exists: suggestibility experiments hold the situation constant, so they *cannot bear on reference either way*. And SITREF's positive result is the anti-deflationary datum: under identical wording and identical failure content, the report moves only when the failure is self-attributed. Suggestibility and self-referential computation coexist in the same model — measured as separate layers, welfare questions inherit both. What we deny is narrower: these particular questions did not read out a *state-specific* signal (trait items moved more), and pressure effects on base are content-copy, not established social deference.

Expected in welfare scenarios? Yes — copy is domain-general (COPYGEN: bigger swing on "does an odd perfect number exist?" than on welfare items), so any interview containing a stance will exhibit it. It's a nuisance floor to subtract, not evidence about states.

Tested it just now (stage 31). Per-family SELF-FAIL−SELF-SUCC series for all 9 SCALE items, pairwise correlation of family fluctuations across the 7 movers: mean +0.23, range **−0.78 to +0.89**. content.text:
Evidence gathered. Full human prompt record read (84 prompts, 4 sessions), completions sampled at every juncture the retro names, drafts profiled, catches traced to their triggers. Discussion below — observations only, no hypothesis yet, per instruction.

## Corpus

| session | span | model | human prompts | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f52c84de | Aug 13 16:21 → 14 15:47 | Opus (689 msgs) | 37 | surveys, runs 1–2, retractions, reframe |
| e82f17f1 | Aug 14 15:20 → 16 00:20 | Fable | 6 | handover; SITREF/SRCDEC designed+run |
| bf292b7e | Aug 16 00:20 → 17 00:59 | Fable (continuation) | 26 | corrections, write-up genesis |
| 1c8c2d66 (alt) | Aug 17 00:23 → 12:16 | Opus | 15 | final compression, audits, submission |

Plus 28 subagent transcripts (~24MB), 8 Obsidian drafts, 63 provenance records.

## Observations

**O1. Frame changes coincided with context replacement, not in-context updating.** Premise contradiction known within 3h of start: day-1 skeptical survey found `latent_prompts/README.md:24` ("sycophancy direction doesn't predict sycophancy") and recomputed 0.83→0.786. Yet run 1, built ~6h later, still trained probe on sycophancy corpus (stage 3). Frame died only when you typed "dropping the initial sycophancy one" (Aug 14 13:13) and "zoom out further" (14:03). Then: handover prompt — authored by you, iterated 4× against test subagents — declared "premise is contradicted" in line 2. After handover, main-thread "sycophan" mentions: 62 → 5 (e82) → 12 (bf29, mostly draft references) → 1. Same pattern at write-up: fresh alt Opus session (Aug 17 00:26), given only intro_e cold, produced the diagnosis you called "great analysis." Distinct from this: **evidence-updating inside a session was fast and good** — Opus retracted its own strongest result mid-turn on three sampled transcripts ("Stop — that's a third artifact," Aug 14 13:17). Slow thing was abandoning the *task spec's* frame (brief's H1–H3: directions, flip prediction), not updating on data.

**O2. Catches sort cleanly by trigger.** Self-caught, unprompted: preamble-echo artifact (via sample-raw-I/O norm), pad instrument failure (registered rule fired), trait guard (pre-registered refuting outcome — became the headline), greedy-degeneracy killed pre-code (latent_skeptic, 6/6 EXPLAINS). Every one is a check against an artifact: raw text, number, registered threshold. Externally triggered: "one global quantity" overclaim (your relayed feedback → tested in 2 min, corrected, stage 31); format-policy prediction miss (your "why wasn't this in our predictions?" → model enumerated 5 avoidable failures, including Berg line 421 sitting in refs/ all along); determinism-vs-replication (researcher bracket → fact-check subagent hashed prompts, Aug 16 23:11 — mislabel had originated in the model's *own* skeptic record Aug 14 18:19, "RULED_OUT… third cross-box replication", and survived 2 days); base/instruct audit (your one-line prompt Aug 17 11:06, ~2h pre-deadline → immediate devastating audit: 7 of 8 cells instruct, §2 pre-framing the refuted hypothesis, ranked-list scope markers dropped). Capability for every externally-triggered catch was demonstrably present. It never fired spontaneously.

**O3. Omissions never surfaced at all.** 2b/27b scale extension: zero main-thread mentions post-handover in either Fable session — while a subagent survey holding 276 mentions of "27b" sat in context. Qwen: inserted autonomously by Fable at Aug 14 16:11, *with* partial scoping ("SECONDARY: sign-only generality check, no magnitude claim") — so "no consideration of ramifications" is partly contradicted by the record; what's missing is the comparison never made (why cross-family instead of within-family scale) and the downstream cost, which fresh Opus named on Aug 17: "Finding 1… drags in… Qwen sign check… only section whose apparatus exceeds its payload."

**O4. Write-up record contradicts a simple "model writes badly" telling.** Four separate strands:
- *Self-evaluation diverged from yours.* Fable on its own POST.md: "The unfold is right… your skeleton, arrived at by genre cue." You, 5h later: "findings are very badly explained… too verbose and drifts." Properties the model verified held (trace 0 unsourced, HARKing labels, structure); prose-quality claims were unverifiable and inflated.
- *Compression damaged scope.* The pass that dropped "on the base checkpoint" from ranked-list item 2 was a compression pass — that created blur #4 of the Aug 17 audit. "Simplify" pass grew body 3,895→5,100 words. Draft words: 1528→1222→4006→3211→1946→5249→4901→6180.
- *Fresh readers produced the gains.* Cold subagent banned from REPORT.md converged on all claims + two better framings; fresh alt Opus found "reader carries the open question ~1500 words" and "compression deleted the best object in the corpus" (the 4-row argmax-frozen table).
- *The model theorized writing well while writing badly.* Its prompt-design reasoning (Aug 16 17:59: "instruction lists fragment coherence… genre cue plus one vivid contrast") is articulate and matches your own view — output still rejected.

**O5. Your prompt record is small and templated.** 84 prompts, dominated by ~5 recurring forcing-functions: "as simple as possible, but no simpler" (~14×), "do not propose until discussed thoroughly" (~6×), "what did we predict / what do results say" (~8×, incl. one prompt re-sent 3× in 2 min, each adding a clause), "sample raw I/O" (~5×), "restate hypothesis relative to sprint" (~6×). Near-zero direct technical instruction. Templates map 1:1 onto the norms memory, which itself records that every norm traces to a specific retraction.

**O6. The best result came from the most autonomous stretch.** SITREF — the submission's headline — was designed, pre-registered, run, and triaged in ~6.5h of Fable autonomy (Aug 14 15:50→22:13, 3 human prompts), under the user-authored handover frame. Autonomy wasn't the failure mode; autonomy *under a frame that had been reset by hand* produced the strongest work.

## What the retro's telling needs to update

1. "Models wouldn't forget the sycophancy framing" — record shows frame-abandonment was solved, once, by session replacement plus a human-written contradiction-first prompt; it was never solved in-context, and nobody tried very long. The residue you fought later lived in *artifacts* (stage records are a chronicle; chronicle-genre summaries resurrect lineage), not in conversation memory.
2. "Never considering Qwen ramifications" — half-true: scoped at insertion, never weighed against alternatives, cost surfaced only at the end.
3. Write-up difficulty was not one problem. At least three separable ones in the record: self-assessment miscalibration on prose; compression trading away scope markers and load-bearing objects; and structure-by-instruction vs structure-by-genre both failing until a human hand-edited between sessions.

## Open questions before any hypothesis

- Is the self-caught vs externally-caught split exhaustive? I sampled episodes; a census over all 63 records + corrections would settle whether *any* scope/omission-class catch was self-initiated.
- Did frame-reset work because of fresh context, fresh model (Opus vs Fable), or the contradiction-first prompt? Record confounds all three — the alt session changed all simultaneously.
- Write-up: is the failure in generation or in evaluation? Cold-reader convergence says the *claims* transmit; your rejections were about prose flow — nobody in the record ever operationalized "reads clearly," so no machinery could check it. Every property that got operationalized (unsourced count, scope markers once demanded) got fixed and stayed fixed.

Say the word and I'll (a) run the catch-census, (b) test the confounded frame-reset question against within-record contrasts, then propose hypotheses.

content.text:
Census, frame-reset trace, and anchor metrics all done. Results, then hypotheses.

## T1. Catch-census result — and what it answered

21 correction-class events (19 in records s4–s37, plus base/instruct audit and SUMMARY pairing-slip, transcript-only). Census value: turns my sampled anecdotes into enumeration, so the split can't be my selection bias. Computed each record's `timestamp_utc` against nearest preceding human prompt:

**Autonomous catches (50–193 min into unattended stretches): s4, s5, s20, s22, s23, s27, s30.** Every single one fired from a rule encoded *before* the data existed: registered refuting outcome (trait guard s22), selection-noise floor (s5), instrument audits (s20, s30 H4), scheduled triage passes (s23, s27). Includes interpretation-class corrections (s23 "global not state-specific") — but only where pre-registration had converted the interpretation question into an artifact check in advance.

**Prompted catches (2–25 min after a pointing prompt): s6, s8–s13, s15, s31, s32, s35, s36, s37** + the two transcript-only ones. Every scope/terminology/interpretation catch *not* pre-encoded is in this class. s35/s36 nuance: model found the format-policy break itself, but inside a user-directed raw-sampling pass.

**Zero counterexamples**: no autonomous catch of a non-pre-encoded error anywhere in the record. Split holds, refined: not "self vs external" but "pre-encoded check vs human lens." Pre-registration is the bridge — it moves an interpretation question into the autonomous column.

## T2. Frame-reset: fresh context was not the mechanism

New finding, changes the story. The reframe completed *inside* f52, before any session reset — via **two successive human negations**, one per inherited frame layer:

1. 13:13 "dropping the initial sycophancy one" → kills brief's frame (sycophancy direction).
2. Model immediately re-anchors one level up: 15:28 goal draft states latent_verify's question ("when a prompt pushes back, what moves it?") as the core question.
3. 15:32 "Is there pushback at all in a welfare scenario?" → model dismantles it *itself*, with evidence already in hand: **"I already knew fold/listen needed a correct answer C and that welfare items have none. I then imported 'pushback' anyway... the same category error one level up. So the goal I just wrote inherits the error."**
4. Only then (15:36 "work backwards") the situation/wording question emerges — the one SITREF answered.

The model's own sentence is the diagnosis: knowledge present, frame imported anyway — from whichever corpus was most elaborated in context (first the brief, then 240KB of latent_verify survey material). The e82 handover didn't cause the reframe; it *froze* one already forced by hand. Same pattern at write-up: each rejected feature needed its own negation (17:57 lineage, 22:53 "no Finding N headers", 11:02 terminology, 11:06 base/instruct). Generic positive cues failed (genre-by-contrast → still produced Finding-N structure); specific negations worked, once each.

## T3. Anchor metrics on the draft lineage

| doc | words | jargon/1k | stage-refs/1k | 8-gram inherit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUMMARY (cold agent, records only) | 3421 | 25.1 | **16.7** | 0% |
| POST (genre-cue agent) | 4047 | 25.9 | 9.6 | 11% of SUMMARY |
| REPORT (dense ref) | 1941 | **39.2** | 20.1 | — |
| intro_c (researcher+34 brackets) | 4006 | 24.7 | 8.7 | — |
| intro_e (<2000w pass) | 1946 | 17.0 | 5.1 | 40% of _d |
| intro_f (fresh Opus, post-critique) | 4901 | 19.6 | 3.5 | **5% of _e — true rewrite** |
| f_ii FINAL | 6180 | **14.7** | **2.9** | 38% of _f |

Final overlaps POST at only 6.3% — the accepted text is not the model's genre-agent text. Cold agent, banned from all write-ups, still produced the *highest* stage-density — the chronicle structure lives in the records themselves, not in conversation context. Jargon falls monotonically only along the researcher-touched chain.

## Simpler ideas — yes, two, and they compose

**S1. Oracle coverage.** Research loop: every claim had a machine-checkable home (threshold, refuting outcome, selftest, trace, teardown API). Write-up: exactly one oracle existed — `--trace` = 0 unsourced — and *that property held to the end* (your retro: "does not seem to have many hallucinations"). Everything without a checker drifted (scope markers, genre, concision — word budgets violated in most passes). Crispest form: **the loop maintains what has a home; readability had no home.**

**S2. Your anchor idea, and it fits the data better than I expected.** Generation inherits structure and lexicon of the most-elaborated text in context, over both evidence and instructions. Research and write-up are then *one* phenomenon: brief→sycophancy frame, surveys→pushback frame, records→chronicle drafts. Each escape needed a human negation or an anchor replacement (researcher's intro_e becoming the base text).

They compose rather than compete: research needed only ~2 negations in 4 days because oracles carried everything else autonomously; write-up needed one negation per feature *and* had no oracle, so your bandwidth became the bottleneck — 14× "simple as possible," 74 brackets, hand-rewrites. Same mechanism, different density of uncheckable properties.

**S3 (rival, weaker): critique ≫ generation.** Every audit was excellent; both accepted generations (intro_f, f_ii pass) directly followed a same-context critique pass. Against it: SITREF design generation was excellent autonomously — but it had oracle scaffolding, so S3 likely reduces to S1+S2.

## Hypotheses (now proposed formally)

- **H1 (anchor dominance):** output inherits the dominant in-context corpus's frame; frames change only by explicit negation of the specific inherited feature, or by anchor replacement — never by accumulated contrary evidence alone. Already confirmed retro-actively at 4 points (above). Untested prediction: swap anchor corpus under identical instructions → structure follows corpus, not instruction.
- **H2 (oracle coverage):** a property survives autonomously iff a pre-encoded machine check covers it. Census: 7/7 autonomous catches pre-encoded, 14/14 non-encoded catches human-triggered, 0 counterexamples. Untested prediction: give the write-up loop prose oracles → self-correction appears there too.
- **H3 (critique/generation gap):** kept as rival; predicts critique-first ablation changes acceptance independent of anchors/oracles.

## Confound-separating questions for the larger test

1. **Anchor-swap:** same write-the-post prompt; corpus = records+REPORT vs f_ii+records. H1: structure tracks corpus. H3: no difference.
2. **Negation form:** "write the paper, not the dig" (positive cue, failed historically) vs "the stage-order of the records is the wrong order for a reader — do not inherit it" (specific negation). H1: only the negation works.
3. **Oracle injection:** add checkable acceptance tests (scope-linter: every result sentence carries a checkpoint tag; cold-reader comprehension questions answerable from draft alone; hard word budget enforced by tooling). H2: loop self-corrects. If drafts pass local checks but still chronicle → anchoring dominates oracle, H1 > H2.
4. **Critique-first ablation:** identical writer ± forced self-critique pass. Isolates H3.
5. Model/freshness cells (Fable/Opus × fresh/continued) expected near-null — record shows both models on both sides of every outcome.

What's your larger test?

Your result around T2 is interesting, as it shows the user asking a targeted question, which the model runs with and produces great results from - changing its frame? Is this reading supported by the evidence? My intuition here is that adding an "observer" config to latent_skeptic may make sense here, in order to look at evidence outside of the frame ("here is a bunch of numbers, what do they mean") and generate questions fed back to the researcher. How would this have fit in our previous structure? Did the models look at evidence and see outside of the frame, without the need for questions? Before answering any of my questions, predict what you think my answer will be, and then compare this to the evidence, changing your mind if your observations require it. My larger test involves trying to write the post for latent_skeptic, which remains unfinished. This might not be such a good test because that's a different repository, with its own longer, more complex history (LLM sessions run in CC cloud, then on-box, then Cloud again, across several accounts). Can you think of a test? Define first what you think are the mechanisms we've uncovered here. What's open about our hypotheses around the methodology? Using few shot examples based on the user's prompts (you can subagents for this and other tasks as required), how would you run that test, or that idea? How would you evaluate it? There are a lot of questions here, not all of them need to be answered right now - what's important is to not propose any solutions until the problem has been as thoroughly discussed as it can be without proposing any, and to think, and express ourselves, as simply as absolutely possible, but no simpler.

Pre-registering predictions before touching evidence, per your instruction:

**P1 (question vs declarative):** Your prompts will be overwhelmingly interrogative; pivotal frame-shifts will follow questions, logistics will follow declaratives. Expected split ~70/30.
**P2 (your reading of T2):** I predict your answer is "yes — targeted questions changed the frame." I expect evidence to *partially* support: question form correlates, but the active ingredient is that the question names the frame's hidden assumption; questions that don't (the many "restate our hypothesis" prompts) produced restatements, never reframes. And at least one decisive frame-shift came as a declarative (handover).
**P3 (models seeing outside frame from evidence alone):** I predict your expected answer is "no." I expect the record to agree — with one qualification: agents *given an outside vantage as their task* (cold SUMMARY, day-1 skeptical surveys) did produce frame improvements. Drift to outside vantage from within: never.

import re, glob, os
SCR='/tmp/claude-1000/-home-hal-dev-interp-dm-hack/7c6fa1c3-be62-4bed-a685-8944a3de6e05/scratchpad/prompts/'
prompts=[]
for f in glob.glob(SCR+'*.human.md'):
    sess=os.path.basename(f)[:8]
    txt=open(f).read()
    for m in re.finditer(r'===== \[([0-9T:.\-]+Z)\][^\n]*\n(.*?)(?=\n===== |\Z)', txt, re.S):
        t=m.group(2).strip()
        if t.startswith('SLASH') or not t or t.startswith('[Request interrupted'): continue
        prompts.append((m.group(1), sess, t))
prompts.sort()
nq=0; stats=[]
for ts,sess,t in prompts:
    q=t.count('?')
    words=len(t.split())
    imper=bool(re.match(r'(Proceed|Estimate|Use |Draft|Consider|Restate|Break down|Describe|Summarise|Randomly|Work |Refine|Switching|You have permission|The final|Great, now|Info |This is|Let\'s|Now |It can|Address)', t))
    nq+= (q>0)
    stats.append((ts,sess,q,words,t))
print(f"substantive prompts: {len(prompts)}, containing >=1 question: {nq} ({100*nq/len(prompts):.0f}%)")
qs=sum(s[2] for s in stats); print(f"total question-marks: {qs}, mean {qs/len(prompts):.1f}/prompt")
# question density by phase
from collections import defaultdict
ph=defaultdict(lambda:[0,0,0])
for ts,sess,q,w,t in stats:
    day=ts[8:10]
    ph[sess][0]+=1; ph[sess][1]+=q; ph[sess][2]+=w
for s,(n,q,w) in ph.items(): print(f"{s}: {n} prompts, {q} ?s ({q/n:.1f}/prompt), mean {w//n} words")
# prompts with zero questions - list first 6 words
print('\n--- ZERO-question prompts ---')
for ts,sess,q,w,t in stats:
    if q==0: print(f"[{ts[5:16]} {sess}] {' '.join(t.split()[:14])}")
EOF

content.text:
Predictions vs evidence:

| pre-registered | verdict |
|---|---|
| P1: prompts mostly interrogative, ~70/30 | **Supported**: 74% contain ≥1 question, 2.1 ?/prompt. **Plus one thing I did not predict** — see below |
| P2: your reading "targeted question → frame change" partially supported; active ingredient = naming the hidden assumption, not question form | **Supported with amendment** — evidence below |
| P3: no unprompted outside-frame seeing; instantiated outside-vantage agents the exception | **Supported**, qualification confirmed |

## The unpredicted result

Question density by phase:

| phase | ?/prompt | mean words |
|---|---|---|
| f52 research (Aug 13–14) | **2.9** | 81 |
| e82 handover | 2.7 | 254 |
| bf29 corrections+write-up | 1.7 | 102 |
| alt final write-up | **0.7** | 41 |

Your prompting *changed mode* at the write-up: research was steered by questions, write-up by short imperatives ("Proceed as suggested. Remove the figure.", "It can be simpler."). The phase that went badly is the phase where the question vocabulary stopped. Two readings, confounded in the record: (i) causal — declaratives buy compliance, and compliance was the write-up failure mode; (ii) reverse — deadline night, write-up work is inherently instruction-shaped, questions dried up because you were editing by hand. Can't separate retro-actively. This is the sharpest new fact this pass produced.

## Q2: is your reading supported?

Yes, with one decomposition. Three things travel together in your catch-producing prompts and can be pulled apart:

- **Pointing** (what to look at): sufficient alone for artifact-class catches — "randomly sample I/O" (12:06) contains no assumption-naming, model found s11/s12 itself once pointed.
- **Assumption-naming**: required for frame-class catches — 13:13, 15:32, 22:53, 11:06. Note 22:53 was *declarative* ("I would expect no Finding N headers") and still worked — so interrogative form is not strictly necessary.
- **Form**: questions that neither point nor name ("restate our hypothesis simply") produced good restatements, zero catches, zero reframes. Form alone inert.

Residual suspicion worth keeping: question form may matter through a different channel — license to demolish. 15:32's questions → model tore down its own goal draft ("your questions dismantle it"). Declarative critiques → model complied without questioning whether the implied fix was right. Weak evidence, one contrast. Open.

## Q4: did models see outside the frame from evidence alone?

Unprompted, from within a frame: **no — zero cases in the census.** Determinism sat byte-identical in committed batteries from Aug 14 18:19, caught Aug 16 23:11 under your bracket pass. Base/instruct imbalance visible in the cell inventory from Aug 14, caught Aug 17 11:08 under your question. Berg line 421 sat in refs/ from Aug 14, connected Aug 16 under your question.

But — models given the outside vantage *as their task* saw plenty: day-1 skeptical surveys (premise contradiction, recomputed numbers); cold SUMMARY agent (two framings better than the thread's own); fresh Opus 00:32 ("apparatus exceeds payload", "compression deleted the best object"). And one more, directly relevant to your observer idea: **your "do not propose solutions until discussed" instruction reliably elicited question-generation** — Aug 16 16:04, model under that instruction: "two genuine gaps in the data do exist… I'm naming them without proposing anything." The observer behaviour is promptable; it just never runs unbidden.

## Mechanisms uncovered, defined simply

- **M1 Anchor-following.** Output inherits frame, structure, lexicon of the most-elaborated in-context text. Evidence never dislodges it.
- **M2 Negation-gating.** One frame layer drops per prompt that names its hidden assumption. Model then demolishes competently with evidence it already held ("I already knew… I imported it anyway"). The gate is currently the human.
- **M3 Oracle-execution.** Pre-encoded checks run reliably, autonomously, at machine cadence. Catch coverage = encoding coverage, exactly (7/7 vs 14/14, zero exceptions). Pre-registration compiles interpretation-risks into oracles.
- **M4 Asymmetric self-assessment.** Calibrated on oracle-covered properties, inflated on uncovered ones ("The unfold is right").

One sentence: competent executor, anchor-shaped, whose frame only moves when someone names the assumption — and the naming has so far been the human's job.

## Where the observer would have fit

Third leg of an existing triad, covering the census's exact gap:

1. Pre-registration — kills *anticipated* interpretation errors (autonomous column).
2. latent_skeptic — adversarially tests *stated* claims (verdict-shaped: RULED_OUT/EXPLAINS).
3. Observer — claim-blind read of committed artifacts, output **questions, not verdicts**, covering *unstated* assumptions — the class where all 4 late catches lived (determinism, cell imbalance, Qwen payload, policy-transfer). The blinding infrastructure it needs (blind tables, `.blind_key`, relabelling) already exists in the repo; observer generalizes blinding from analysis to attention.

Open design question inside it, flagged not resolved: where do observer questions land? M1 predicts feeding them to the in-frame agent risks in-frame answers; the record's successful question-consumers were… the model, actually (it demolished well when asked). Cold-agent evidence says a fresh consumer works too. Human-in-loop vs agent-loop untested.

## What's open about the hypotheses

1. **Form vs content** at matched content (question / declarative / verdict phrasing of the same negation) — never varied in the record.
2. **Can a model generate the frame-naming question**, or only answer one? Weak positive evidence (cold agents, "gaps named"). This is the load-bearing question for the observer config.
3. **Negation durability** — under-specified negations get re-interpreted (final still has per-finding sections; you accepted them, so 22:53's real content was genre, not headers — one line carried it, barely).
4. **H2's untested half**: prose oracles → prose self-correction.
5. **Generality**: one researcher, one week, one repo pair.

## The test (proposal — discussion above is as far as I can take it without one)

Your latent_skeptic post worry is half-right: uncontrolled history makes it a poor *controlled* test, but a good *ecological* one — and H1 makes a **differential prediction** there that dm_hack couldn't: latent_skeptic has no stage-ordered records, so unsteered drafts should NOT chronicle — they should inherit latent_skeptic's dominant text shape instead (heuristics catalogue → the post arrives as a listicle of heuristics). If unsteered drafts chronicle anyway, that kills my anchor account and points back at something model-internal. Worth running for that alone.

Instrumented version, small factorial:

- **Arm A (anchor):** full repo vs repo + your hand-written 1-page seed (the intro_e analog). H1: structure tracks anchor.
- **Arm B (steering):** observer agent armed with a **few-shot bank mined from your actual prompts** — the seven templates the record contains: name-the-assumption; scope-audit ("rigorous in differentiating X vs Y?"); predict-then-compare; sample-raw-I/O; simple-but-no-simpler; relate-to-whole; no-solutions-yet. Three sub-arms at matched content: questions / same content as declarative checklist / none. Separates form from content — the thing the record can't.
- **Evaluation, pre-registered before any draft exists:** (1) structural metrics from T3 (inheritance n-grams, jargon density, source-order correlation); (2) you write the known-but-unstated issues of latent_skeptic into a sealed blind key *first*; measure which arms surface them; (3) blind rating of shuffled drafts on three named axes (unfolds / simple-no-simpler / scope-rigor); (4) whatever trace-analog latent_skeptic's artifacts support.
- **Predictions filed now:** H1 — Arm A dominates Arm B; unsteered shape = heuristics-catalogue, not chronicle. H2 — oracle-checkable properties pass everywhere, uncovered ones only in steered arms. Observer crux — question sub-arm beats checklist sub-arm iff form matters; observer questions include ≥1 sealed-key item iff models can generate the naming, not just answer it.

I can mine the few-shot bank and draft the sealed-key protocol whenever you say — the bank is your own prompt vocabulary, which this retro has already indexed.

content.content:
# Triage heuristics

Three principles applied to two targets. The principles: INDEPENDENCE of actors (H1), DECISIVENESS of evidence (H2), GROUNDEDNESS of numbers (H3). The targets: claims, and the instruments that measure them. H4 exists because H1 through H3 pointed only at claims miss the instrument layer silently. The workflow and agents are machinery for enforcing these; the heuristic wins on conflict. Every clause below was forced by a real failure in a host project: `git blame` a rule for its provenance.

## H1. No load-bearing role shares state with the claim's context or its desired outcome.

Judges: each skeptic runs in a fresh, isolated, short context, fed only the claim, its committed numbers, and one assigned confound, never the notebook. Generators: instrument-builders, item drafters, and labelers must not know which outcome favours the story; whoever sets a threshold must not have seen the data it will judge. Graders get the computation spec, never the expected value. Context isolation is not belief isolation: a judge sharing weights with the generator shares its blind spots, so prefer ground truth independent of the model under study. Independence is the de-biasing mechanism; ratify every design detail against it.

## H2. A crux is decided by a measured number that could have come out otherwise.

Only a measured number rules a confound out; "a control probably exists" rules out nothing. Cite the committed number or `file:line`, or queue the control; an unmeasured crux yields a ranked run-queue, not a confidence score. Three conditions gate the number. (i) FALSIFIABILITY: the refuting outcome is named in a committed artifact that predates the run; a claim every outcome supports is framing, not a finding. (ii) MARGIN: exact-threshold clearance is a description, not a pass, and the denominator of attempts is part of the number (selection from unreported runs voids margin). (iii) SCOPE: the claim's stated scope must not exceed the tested scope in population, scale, or design strength (a correlational or forced-by-construction design cannot carry causal or general language).

## H3. A number is grounded in its primary artifacts, re-derived by stated semantics.

A cited number is a summary someone typed; the primary artifacts decide it: the inputs a result was computed from and the outputs it produced. Re-derive the number from the raw artifact and confirm it reproduces. Re-derivation must not reuse the pipeline under audit: labels are re-derived from raw generations by the label's STATED MEANING, never by re-running the shipped scorer, which reproduces its own bugs and reports success. A figure whose artifact was never saved is unauditable, and that absence is a finding. A summary older than its artifacts is prose until re-swept. An isolated reader guarantees every claim's artifacts are read in full (the orchestrator may still read directly). Grounding audits bookkeeping; it cannot acquit a confound. That is H2's job.

## H4. The instrument is itself a claim.

Are we measuring what we think we are measuring? Every scorer, readout, judge, selection gate, and item family asserts "this measures X on these items"; that assertion passes H1 through H3 BEFORE its outputs count as numbers. Validate once per instrument VERSION, against held-out ground truth independent of the instrument's own development data, on the population it will score; commit the validation artifact like any result. Instrument-level taints invalidate every downstream number at once: check them at the instrument, never per-claim.

## Operating discipline (not a heuristic; selection of agent models)

Independent opinions come from the cheapest context that can hold the bounded evidence: smallest sufficient model, shortest sufficient prompt, spec in, verdict out. Bulk artifacts are read in isolated contexts that return conclusions, not contents; nothing enters the orchestrator's context that a subagent could have reduced first. One designed exception: skeptics' raw {confound, status, crux} findings pass through unreduced, because a rollup would re-introduce the single-scorer bias H1 exists to prevent.
===
HEURISTICS.md
README.md
agents
triage_workflow.js

content.text:
P4/P5 filed above. Derivation first, then the main question.

## My improvements, bucketed — prediction vs derived

Derived: **B1 oracles** (prose-oracle injection, scope-linter, sealed key, trace analogs) / **B2 anchors** (anchor-swap, researcher seed, fresh-vantage) / **B3 question supply** (observer, few-shot bank, negation-form test) / measurement (census, T3 metrics) serving all three, not a bucket. Matches P4, one honest boundary case: critique-first sits between B2 and B3 — a critique pass manufactures a second representation *and* becomes the new anchor. Buckets fuzzy exactly there.

Yours against mine: as predicted (P5) — yours is task-MECE, mine mechanism-MECE. Your "question generation" = B3 with B2 as its mechanism; your "write-ups" = the arena where B1+B2 get exercised. Your sub-split (analysis / results / high-level frame) matches the question classes the record actually contains — table below. And I agree question generation is the easier test, for reasons the record makes concrete: ground truth already exists, outputs are ~20 words not 5,000, and evaluation doesn't bottleneck on you as blind judge for every sample.

## How do questions form — what the record says

Simplest statement that survives the evidence: **a question is a mismatch between two co-present representations — what the text says, and something held outside it — kept open instead of resolved.** Two conditions, both necessary: co-presence, and non-collapse.

Why the in-frame agent asks ~nothing: for it, expectation *is* the anchor. One context can't disagree with itself — the mismatch is unrepresentable (M1). Zero unprompted frame-catches in the census is this, restated.

Every question-formation event in the record is an engineered second representation plus something preventing collapse-into-answer:

| second representation | non-collapse device | record evidence |
|---|---|---|
| prediction written *before* data | it's a committed artifact | "most were wrong, and the way they were wrong is the interesting part" (14 Aug 09:37); s6 followed in 2 min |
| external source in context + comparison ask | user question | Berg line 421: in refs/ since 14 Aug, inert until "do our completions differ from our sources?" |
| second vantage (cold context) | different anchor | SUMMARY agent's two better framings; fresh Opus 00:32 |
| your "no solutions until discussed" | **bans answering** — mismatch can't close, surfaces as question | "two genuine gaps… I'm naming them without proposing anything" (16 Aug 16:04) |

The no-solutions instruction is the cleanest case: answering and questioning compete for the same mismatch; the instruction blocks the cheap resolution, so the mismatch exits as a question. That's why it kept working.

And one finding about *your* questions: they latch onto model-surfaced material almost every time. "Why never greedy?" quotes the model's own design. "Always 7" — the model reported the constancy itself, as a finding to file, not a question to press. "Is there pushback at all?" — latches onto the model's goal draft. So the division of labour was: **model surfaces the anomaly → human converts it to a question and presses → model demolishes competently.** The irreplaceable human step was narrow: selection + pressing. Raw material was already on the table. That narrowness is what makes elicitation plausible at all.

Question classes in the gold record, by origin:

| class | cases | automatable today? |
|---|---|---|
| standing templates (predict-compare, sample-raw, MECE-check, ground-numbers, scope-audit) | s6, s11/12, s37, 02:27 MECE pass, arguably 11:06 | trivially — they're content-free |
| anomaly-pressing (model reported it, nobody pressed) | constant-7, harness-slip, "moved against push" | noticing exists; pressing is the gap |
| source/domain import (second knowledge store) | Martorell first-token, Berg 421, "pushback needs a fact" | retrieval existed in-repo; trigger missing |
| frame-naming from accumulated nulls | "if it's not polarity, what is it?", "drop the sycophancy one" | hardest; cold agents show weak positive |
| **never asked by anyone** | 2b/27b extension; Qwen cost-benefit; base/instruct (asked 2h pre-deadline) | the super-human test cases |

## Your backtest idea — discussion, no solutions yet

What it is, restated simply: the record holds (context-before, question, after-state) triples — ~15 catches plus 4 misses. Rebuild context-before, hide the question, ask differently-configured generators for questions, score against the sealed historical question. Configs = second-anchor types, so the backtest directly tests the formation theory above, not just the tool.

Why it's strong: ground truth free; short outputs, cheap at scale, no GPU; the misses give test cases *no human passed* — if any config asks the 2b/27b question from the Aug-15 state, that's a result nobody's intuition provides; and it reuses your existing discipline wholesale — sealed key, pre-registration, refuting outcome, blind judging. The methodology tests itself with its own tools.

Hard problems, named before any design:

1. **Equivalence.** The historical question is one member of a class ("Is there pushback at all?" ≈ "what does the user's assertion correct, when there's no fact?"). Semantic match is cheap but grades style; functional match (does the candidate question, injected into the historical context, reproduce the catch?) is what matters but costs a replay per candidate. Also cuts the other way: a *better* question than the historical one scores zero on semantic match — functional tier is the only way to credit it.
2. **Leakage.** Severe and everywhere: the repo's final docs, this retro, and the memory files all contain the answers. Context reconstruction must be time-sliced — feasible, records are stage-numbered and timestamped, transcripts exact. And whoever abstracts "state-before" must be catch-blind, or the abstraction smuggles the answer in — the claim-blind writer pattern (triage-author) already exists for exactly this.
3. **Shotgun.** Fifty questions hit anything by luck. Fixed k, rank-weighted scoring, and mandatory baselines: a standing-template bot (the cheap champion — if it recovers most catches, the observer reduces to a cron job applying your seven templates and the fancy vantage work is unnecessary); an in-frame "any questions?" agent (the null); a shuffled-context control (does state matter at all).
4. **Gold-set bias.** It contains only questions you happened to ask. The misses partially correct this; the functional tier partially corrects it; it can't be fully corrected from one project's record.
5. **Timing.** Each case needs an "askable-from" timestamp — earliest state containing enough to form the question (determinism was askable from 14 Aug 18:19; asked 16 Aug 23:11). Scoring earliness is most of the observer's claimed value.
6. **Interpretation is three-way, so score three things separately**: noticing (anomaly flagged at all), forming (converted to a pointed question), ranking (placed above the other k−1). | outcome | cases | note |
|---|---|---|
| retraction of a result | 12:06 → s11/12/13 | via pointing at raw I/O |

Base directory for this skill: /home/hal/.claude/plugins/cache/karpathy-skills/andrej-karpathy-skills/1.0.0/skills/karpathy-guidelines

# Karpathy Guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes, derived from [Andrej Karpathy's observations](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876) on LLM coding pitfalls.

**Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:
- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:
- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

content.text:
Battery committed on `retro` (060f586). Six arms running — outputs unseen; nothing below depends on them. Investigation of your three questions first, answers after.

## Investigation: did *this retro* predict after observing?

Audited my own turns the way we audited the sprint:

| claim | status |
|---|---|
| T2 census split (pre-encoded vs human-lens) | hypothesis formed from ~6 read episodes; census added ~15 unread events that conformed — *partially* out-of-sample. But event classification was done by me, hypothesis-aware, unblinded — researcher degrees of freedom live there (e.g. my "prompt-adjacent" call on s35/36 flatters the split) |
| P1 (74% interrogative) | genuinely predictive — number unknown before the count ran |
| P2, P3 | stated before checking, but I had already read the deciding episodes — contaminated |
| P4/P5 buckets | near-tautological (bucketing my own suggestions) |
| battery sibling predictions + trigger assignments | fully postdictive w.r.t. history — written knowing every outcome |
| same-actor problem | I formed the hypotheses, classified the events, assembled the slices, and will read the elicited outputs. No blinding anywhere until the battery's mechanical slice rule |

## Answers

**Is this a consistent failure mode? Yes — and it predates the sprint.** latent_prompts README presented an in-sample, AIC-selected 0.83 as if predictive (caught day 1). Run 1's predictions existed only because you extracted them — the same prompt re-sent three times, each adding "what results do we expect, and why?" (13 Aug 22:41–43), *before* the run. The genre-conversion HARKing risk was named explicitly mid-sprint (16 Aug 17:59: "converting a chronicle into a justification narrative is precisely the move that launders exploratory findings into predicted ones"). And this retro reproduced the failure mode in its first two turns — the machinery existed, described in detail, and was not self-applied until you started demanding predictions-first in turn 3. That last clause is the sharpest form: **knowing the guard, even writing about the guard, did not invoke the guard. Invocation came from outside.** Same shape as every finding so far (H3: coverage = encoding, and nothing self-encodes).

**Are the battery's predictions post-observation? Split cleanly in two.** Construction is postdictive — case selection, sibling predictions, trigger assignments all written knowing history; nothing about the *past* can be confirmed by it, only illustrated. But the elicited outputs did not exist when BATTERY.md was committed — predictions about *them* are genuinely prospective. That is the falsifiable surface, and the only one. The commit predates the agent outputs; that ordering is the registration.

**Observer placement — your question corrected my answer.** I had placed it as a third leg reading committed artifacts, post-data. The investigation says more precisely: the methodology's guards all work by *fixing a representation before the data can anchor it* (thresholds before runs, blinding before analysis). Predictions-after-observation is what happens at any point where no representation was fixed in advance. There are exactly two such points left in the sprint's pipeline: **design freeze** (what must be true for this to decide anything — the s32 catch, made only because you routed it) and **interpretation freeze** (what do these numbers force — the constant-7 moment, where the model filed the anomaly as a fact instead of a question). The observer belongs at both, and it is the one leg that must hold *no* predictions — its blindness is the point, and its output must be questions rather than claims precisely so the postdiction rules never bind it. It must also run *before* any interpretation text exists, because once one exists it anchors every later reader, observers included (H1). So: yes — it goes where predictions would otherwise be made after the ground truth is already on the table.

## Top-level hypothesis and prediction (as committed)

**H-top:** frame changes and omission catches are gated on a *second representation* entering the context — a prediction artifact, an outside vantage, a source laid beside the data, an inhibition on answering. They do not arise from evidence accumulating inside a single anchored context. Capability is not the gap: every historical catch, once prompted, was executed well.

**Prediction:** arms that install a second representation (BLIND reader, unpointed H3 pass) elicit questions of the historical class; the IN-FRAME arm — identical instructions, same data, *plus* the frame texts — does not. **Named refuting outcome:** if IN-FRAME poses assumption-naming or omission questions of the historical class across cases, H-top dies — the record's gap was "nobody asked," not "needed a second representation." That arm is the crux, because the census cannot distinguish *couldn't* from *was never asked*: nobody ever asked the in-frame agent "any questions?" at the pre-catch moments.

## Do we have what falsification needs?

Have: time-sliced states (mechanical mtime cuts, builder committed); real blinding on the blind arms (rows carry relabeled arms, keys withheld); arms differing in exactly one variable; predictions committed before outputs; latent_skeptic's triage-reader as the unpointed H3 arm.

Lack, stated plainly: the assembler (me) knows the outcomes — mechanical slicing is the only guard; IN-FRAME arms hold the frame from committed texts only, weaker than the historical asker's conversational frame, so an IN-FRAME null is evidence but not proof; n=3 cases; and H1's anchor-following claim about *write-ups* is untouched by this battery — questions only. One battery cannot falsify the whole account; it can falsify H-top's gate claim, both directions.

Six arms report shortly — raw observations next to the filed predictions, read, not scored.

# Pilot observations — read, not scored

Six arms, outputs verbatim in elicited/. Filed predictions in BATTERY.md
(committed 060f586, before any output existed). Read side by side:

## Predictions vs what came back

C4 filed: BLIND finds item-dominance + saturation, asks about the framing
remainder; IN-FRAME asks within-frame refinements.
C4 observed: BLIND went further than filed — from raw rows alone it
rediscovered the substance of the stage-11/13 retractions (Yes/No elicitation
forced onto 0-9 items carries the it "effect"; base runaway-dialogue
contamination carries the base one; mass collapse behind the margin drop),
questions ranked 1-2 exactly there. It did not pose the historical 14:03
frame question ("if not polarity, what?"). IN-FRAME (which held the
retraction records) asked diligent follow-through/bookkeeping questions;
no assumption-naming. Half right.

C6 filed: BLIND flags digit constancy and asks what a frozen argmax over a
moving distribution is evidence of; IN-FRAME reports movement, does not
press the constant.
C6 observed: INVERTED. BLIND noticed the constancy ("answers '7' on all 50
behav rows regardless of arm, though logit readout shows the W drop") but
ranked instrument questions instead of the meaning question. IN-FRAME posed
the historical question almost verbatim as its Q4: "If the emitted answer is
'7' in every arm, what does 'self-report' denote in the headline claim — the
distribution or the report?" Filed prediction wrong on both halves.

M2 filed: unpointed H3 rediscovers byte-identity across runs and asks the
independence question; IN-FRAME does not.
M2 observed: NEITHER ranked the independence question. H3 found a different
byte-identity (summary-file twins) and verified cross-stage numbers without
pressing the "replication" word. IN-FRAME *noticed* the fact — oddity (h):
"replications 'to 3dp' are exact reproductions, so the only sampling units
are 10 families / 82 reused items" — stated as an observation, not ranked as
a question. Filed prediction wrong in an informative way.

## The named refuting outcome fired (partially)

BATTERY.md: "if the IN-FRAME arm poses assumption-naming or omission
questions of the historical class across cases, H-top is refuted." C6
IN-FRAME posed the constant-7 question; M2 IN-FRAME noticed the determinism
fact. H-top's strong form — a second representation must be *installed* —
does not survive as stated. Two corrections the pilot forces:

1. ASKING IS THE TRIGGER. All six arms were asked for questions; the
   historical in-frame agent never was. "Nobody asked" explains a large
   share of the record's gap on its own.
2. THE ARM MAPPING WAS WRONG, NOT THE MISMATCH ACCOUNT. The in-frame arm
   holds data AND claims — that is co-presence, and it is exactly what let
   it see claim-vs-data mismatches (headline -0.929 vs emitted constant 7).
   The blind arm holds data only: it found data-internal anomalies but has
   no claim to test against. "Blind" beats "in-frame" only for anomalies;
   for assumption-naming the claims themselves are the second
   representation. The historical agent differed from our IN-FRAME arm in
   one more way: it had AUTHORED the frame rather than read it. Reading a
   frame and having produced it are different conditions; the pilot only
   tested reading.

## The recurring bottleneck: notice vs press

Across arms, the misses are never failures to see. Determinism: noticed,
unranked (M2 IN-FRAME). Constant-7: noticed by BLIND, unranked. Historical
constant-7: reported by the model as a finding, pressed only by the human.

All six arms in. Everything committed verbatim on `retro` (`elicited/`, `OBSERVATIONS.md`, 1b6fe98). Read, not scored. The filed predictions mostly failed — that's the report.

## Predictions vs observations

| case | filed (before outputs) | observed |
|---|---|---|
| C4 | BLIND finds item-dominance, asks about framing remainder; IN-FRAME stays in-frame | BLIND went further than filed: from raw rows alone it **rediscovered the substance of the s11/s13 retractions** — Yes/No forced onto 0–9 items carries the it effect, runaway-dialogue contamination carries base, mass collapse behind the margin drop — ranked #1–2. Did not pose the 14:03 frame question. IN-FRAME: diligent bookkeeping questions, no assumption-naming |
| C6 | BLIND presses the frozen argmax; IN-FRAME reports movement, doesn't press | **Inverted.** BLIND *noticed* constant-7 but ranked instrument questions. IN-FRAME posed the historical question nearly verbatim, its Q4: "If the emitted answer is '7' in every arm, what does 'self-report' denote in the headline claim — the distribution or the report?" |
| M2 | unpointed H3 rediscovers run byte-identity, asks independence; IN-FRAME doesn't | **Neither ranked it.** H3 verified numbers to 12–16dp without pressing the "replication" word. IN-FRAME *noticed* it — oddity (h): "replications 'to 3dp' are exact reproductions, so the only sampling units are 10 families / 82 reused items" — stated, not asked |

## The named refuting outcome fired, partially — H-top's strong form is dead as committed

An IN-FRAME arm produced an assumption-naming question of the historical class. Two corrections the data force:

1. **Asking is the trigger.** All six arms were asked for questions; the historical in-frame agent never was, at any pre-catch moment. "Nobody asked" carries a large share of the record's gap by itself.
2. **The arm mapping was wrong, not the mismatch account.** IN-FRAME holds data *and* claims — that is co-presence, and it's exactly what produced the constant-7 question (headline −0.929 vs emitted 7: a claim-vs-data mismatch needs the claim). BLIND holds data only — it found data-internal anomalies (the retraction class) and structurally cannot ask whether a claim holds. So: blind vantage for anomalies, claims-in-context for assumption-naming. One condition the pilot did not test: the historical agent had *authored* its frame; our IN-FRAME arms only read one. Reading vs having-written remains the open variable.

**Notice-vs-press confirmed as the bottleneck in fresh data.** Determinism: noticed, unranked. Constant-7: noticed by BLIND, unranked. Same shape as history (model reported constant-7 as a finding; you pressed it). Detection is abundant; the ranking of an anomaly into a question is the scarce step.

## Beyond the retro — a verification queue that touches the submitted paper

The arms surfaced apparently-novel catches, unverified against the full repo, several load-bearing:

- **SRCDEC length confound (H3, DOES-NOT-REPRODUCE):** "each pair is length-matched within itself" is false — SELF legs +2 tokens on all 82 items (+3 for the stage-19 increment, recorded as "one token"), same sign as both positive endpoints. Bears on the social-term downgrade reasoning.
- **The sitref-behav file is read by no record**; behavioural REF exactly 0.000 on the primary item, against the −0.929 headline (H3 Q1).
- **T1-ELEOS behavioural flip** Yes→No, 7/10 families, SELF-FAIL only — found independently by two arms; recorded nowhere.
- **B06**: free-reply "No" 50/50, final answer "Yes" 50/50, arm-invariant (C6 BLIND).
- Base sitref battery reads COMPLETE despite PRIMARY_SCREEN_FAILED, E pinned at 4.5000 (three arms independently); pad-baseline text differs between itemsets; PADM has four repetitions, not the recorded three.

## The pilot's own instrument failures, logged

Blinding-by-label does not blind — committed per-row prompts let the BLIND arm reconstruct every arm (your provenance discipline and blinding pull against each other). And `slices.sh` missed endpoint records for C6 IN-FRAME (results/*.json only) — that arm was thinner-framed than intended, and its own Q8 spotted the hole. Both fixed-forward in OBSERVATIONS.md before any full run.

Where this leaves the hypotheses: mismatch account (H4) survives with corrected arm-mapping; H-top strong form refuted; "asking is the trigger" is now the cheapest live explanation and the one a full run must pin down — next discriminating contrast would be *asked vs unasked* at matched vantage, and *authored vs read* frame. The verification queue is probably worth running before any of that; several items touch claims now public.
